newsitem.title: USA: Hutchinson Tech shares dip after Tuesday surge.
newsitem.headline: Hutchinson Tech shares dip after Tuesday surge.

text.p: Shares of Hutchinson Technology Inc fell 1-1/2 to 70-3/4 Wednesday morning as investors cashed in some profits tallied during Tuesday's strong rally, analysts said.
On Tuesday the shares jumped 19-1/2 to 72-1/4 after the company said it expected first-quarter earnings well above analysts' estimates.
"I think you got a little profit-taking, and I suspect management also is trying to temper peoples' excitement," said Clinton Morrison, senior analyst, John Kinnard & Co.

"It's not surprising to see a pullback somewhat," said Cody Acree, analyst, Olde Discount Corp. "But I definitely don't think there's any negative news or negative feelings that are pressuring the stock."
Minnesota-based Hutchinson, which makes suspension assemblies for computer disk drives, said Tuesday it looked for fiscal first quarter 1997 net sales of $104 to $109 million.
It said it expected earnings of $1.50 to $1.90 per share. This compares to $0.51 a year ago after a $0.69 charge, and contrasts with First Call's consensus estimate of $0.71.
Early on Wednesday Hutchinson Chief Executive Wayne Forun told Reuters he expects demand to remain stable to strong through next March.
